RAW development

Edit RAW files from your camera and phone directly, on Immich or on your device, with everything the sensor recorded: more room in the highlights and shadows, and color without loss. A RAW opens tools of its own, such as development profiles and Calibration, and the export matches what you see.
Remove tool
Paint over what you want gone: Remove fills it from its surroundings, and Heal and Clone copy from an area you choose. Visualize spots reveals sensor dust hidden in a sky.
Sharpening and noise reduction
In the Detail panel, Sharpening brings out edges and leaves smooth areas alone. Noise Reduction removes grain and color blotches from high-ISO photos.
Histogram and clipping
The Light panel shows the histogram, and its triangles paint what is clipped on the photo: shadows in blue, highlights in red. Highlights are stronger in new edits.
Optics and calibration
The new Optics panel corrects lens vignetting and removes purple and green fringes along edges. On RAW files, Calibration adjusts the shadows tint and each primary color.
Live Photos and Motion Photos
A photo with motion shows up once in the library, with a badge. In the detail, press and hold it to see the motion.
In the background
Saving to the gallery, sending to Immich and Show your edit keep going when you leave the app, with a notification that lets you cancel. The video now draws the masks and shows the crop closing in.
More improvements
Edited RAW files from Immich show in the library as you left them; when it is still an approximation, the detail says so and shows the final version.
Sharing asks whether to send the original or the edited photo.
Filters work inside each album.
A stack shows your latest export when the edit has changed since.
An older RAW edit moves to the current development in one tap.
The forum is always at hand in Support, with a notice of new replies.
Each server address’s options no longer get mixed up with the new address’s.
A faster library, and large RAW files that export without running out of memory.
Protected servers (in testing)

Under Advanced, when you connect an Immich server, add headers, such as a Cloudflare Access token, or import a client certificate; it also works with your own certificate authority. It is in testing: tell us what doesn’t work with your setup.
Errors that explain

When a proxy or a certificate stops the connection, the app says so, instead of “key rejected” or “server unreachable”. The support report names the kind of failure, never the address, the key or the headers.
Support and diagnostics
In Settings, describe a problem, review the report of the last 24 hours and open an email to support with it attached. The history stays on the device, and nothing is sent until you have reviewed it.
Forum from support
Share questions, ideas and bugs with the community from the support card, with a title, a category and up to four images. Review everything before posting, with or without an IMAGO account.
Clearer Settings

Settings are now grouped into IMAGO account, Preferences, Libraries, Support and diagnostics, and About. Each category opens and closes from its header, and the connection test shows its result next to the server.
Improvements and fixes

Before sending an edit from an external Immich library, the app tells you it may show up apart from the original. When an album or a search fails to load, it shows the error with “Try again” instead of the photos from the previous view.
Color and light masks
In Masks, select a color or a luminance range to adjust only those parts of your photo. Tap or drag to sample, refine the selection and combine it with other masks.
Draw over your photos
In the composer, draw over photos with the pen or marker. The tool stays open when you lift your finger or stylus, and stylus pressure is preserved in your strokes.
Floating controls
Drawing and shape settings now sit in a floating panel you can drag out of the way. Reuse colors from your composition or pick a color directly from the page with the eyedropper.
Shapes with a gesture
In the composer, tap to place a shape or drag to draw squares, circles, lines and arrows. Adjust it afterwards and let it extend beyond the page edges to build your layout.
Improvements and fixes

Bring back the editor panel without closing the mask tool, and zoom into the composer page with two fingers. We fixed freezes when drawing or reframing the background and improved tool switching and the eraser indicator.
Show your edit
In Export, make a vertical video of your edit: the sliders move, the photo follows them, and the before and after comes at the end. Pick one of three styles, add a title and share it right away.
Masks that combine
Add, subtract or intersect shapes in a mask, and set each mask’s Amount from 0 to 200%. Duplicate a mask, or duplicate it inverted, and use up to eight per photo.
Paint the mask
The Brush paints the area to adjust, the Eraser fixes it, and Auto Mask keeps it inside the edges. Each with Size, Feather, Flow and Density.
Video in compositions

With a video selected, the timeline shows the page’s videos: drag them to move them, trim them by their ends and choose which ones you hear. When exporting, pick the quality and see the file size first.
Light and lens

In white balance, Auto removes the color cast of the light, and a recipe with it looks for the light again in each photo it is applied to. In Perspective, Distortion straightens the lines the lens has curved.
Copy only what you want
Copying or saving a recipe shows what it carries, panel by panel, and you choose down to each slider. Crop, perspective and masks start switched off, so they don’t spoil the photo you paste onto.
Only the albums you want
In Settings, choose which albums appear in All, so screenshots and WhatsApp images stop mixing with your photos. In the albums grid, a long press hides an album, and Show all brings them back.
Improvements and fixes

Sending edits to an Immich 3 server now works, an edited background in the composer keeps its edits, and a new mask starts in the part of the photo you can see. Plus several optimizations and small fixes.
One gallery
Your phone and Immich in one timeline, without duplicates. Albums on both sides to create, organize and delete, plus Trash and Archive.
Find your photos

In Immich, search for what is in them (“beach”, “birthday cake”) or browse them on the Map and by People. On this day brings back this day in other years, and Info shows the camera, the address and who is there.
Stacks
Immich stacks show by their cover, and you can create and manage them in the app, phone photos included. An edit exported to Immich becomes the cover of its original’s stack.
Straight lines
In Crop, perspective correction straightens buildings and horizons, and Upright does it for you: Auto, Level, Vertical, Full or with guides you draw. Crops, rotations and flips show in Immich too.
Precise color
The tone curve opens large over the photo, with curves for red, green and blue. White balance is stronger, with an eyedropper to pick a grey in the photo.
A tidier editor

The bottom bar is always there, the panel can be dragged, and scrolling the list no longer changes values by accident. Recipes get Favorites, Recent, hearts on filters and collections to choose from when saving.
Part of your phone
Open photos and videos from other apps with IMAGO, use it as a picker and save to the IMAGO album. Select several photos to share, rotate, archive or add to an album.
Recipes can now be edited: tap one in the recipe library to open it over a sample photo, adjust it and save. Swipe to see it on other photos.
Built-in filters open the same way, and saving one makes your own copy.
New recipe, Duplicate and Delete, in the recipe library and inside the editor.

Your Immich API key no longer needs write permissions: reading and downloading photos is enough. Without the others, only the tools that use them stop working, and the app tells you which one is missing and where to add it.
When you connect an Immich server, the app lists the required and optional permissions separately, explains what each one is for and says which are missing.
Recipe previews show their sample photos again, instead of empty tiles.
Settings now show the installed version and what changed in it.
Names the app creates on its own, such as for exports and sync copies, now follow the app language.
